- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.28) in recent days, reduce forecasted price by 5–10% to account for downward pressure.  
- If model shows a sharp spike (e.g., >10% above recent mean) followed by a forecast decline, reduce the peak by 10–15% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), adjust forecast to reflect gradual decline rather than abrupt drop.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.17 for 3+ days), slightly increase forecasted mean but cap at 10% above recent 18-day average.  
- If forecasted price is consistently above true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast by 5–8% to avoid overconfidence bias.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating positive/negative swings, model should not overreact to single-day sentiment shifts — smooth transitions with 1–2-day lag.
